chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from a man, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Do not ask about things which have not been revealed to you; if they are revealed to you, they will trouble you.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Quranic verse 'Do not ask about things which if declared to you may trouble you' according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'sukn al-ahwal' (tranquility of hearts) by linking the prohibition of inquiring about undefined matters to the potential for anxiety if they were revealed. It reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that divine wisdom often withholds specific details to preserve the spiritual peace of the believers, a concept deeply rooted in the exegesis of Surah al-Ma'idah. The narration serves as a practical guide for avoiding unnecessary speculation that leads to doubt or distress.

en.hubeali: H 14696 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from a man, who has narrated:
